intended_object: The underlying function of the canonical projection G → G(p) from a profinite group to its maximal pro-p quotient G(p) = lim G/U, where U runs over the open normal subgroups with G/U a finite p-group. It sends x to the compatible family (xU)_U. This comes from the docstring and from its use in `eta`.
explanation:
The maximal pro-p quotient `product p G` is built as `limit (diagram p G)` in `ProfiniteGrp`. Here `diagram p G` sends each open normal subgroup U with G/U a p-group to the finite group G/U, and sends an inclusion U ≤ V to the induced quotient map G/U → G/V. An element of this limit is a compatible family of cosets.

`etaFn` sends x to the family U ↦ xU, that is, `QuotientGroup.mk x` at every U. Compatibility holds by `rfl`, because the transition maps are `QuotientGroup.map` of the identity. This is exactly the canonical map x ↦ (xU)_U from G to G(p).

The library then bundles it as the continuous homomorphism `eta` and proves it has dense range. That is the standard behaviour of the canonical projection to an inverse limit of quotients; since G is compact, the map is in fact surjective.

The setting (a profinite group G and a prime p) is the natural one for this notion. Mathlib has no maximal pro-p quotient construction to compare it with.
